transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… what made me finally come in is how I feel after I have these eating episodes. It’s not just that I ate too much or whatever. It’s like afterward I feel really gross, and just so disappointed in myself, like I should have been able to stop or have more control.

And then I kind of sit with it and make it worse in my head. I’ll write in my journal afterward, and it turns into me writing these really awful things about myself. Like I’m angry at myself, or disgusted with myself, and I know that sounds dramatic, but in the moment it feels really true. I just don’t want to keep feeling like that after it happens.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate for what you’ve eaten, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing extra exercise?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, not in the way you’re describing. I don’t make myself throw up or anything like that, and I’m not, like, taking stuff after to try to undo it.

The exercise thing is a little harder for me to answer because sometimes I’ll think, like, “Okay, tomorrow I need to be better,” or “I should move more,” but I don’t really have some planned punishment workout or anything. It’s more the thoughts afterward, feeling awful about it, not so much doing something specific to make up for it.
How often do these eating episodes happen, and do they usually happen in response to a specific feeling, like stress or sadness?

It’s been pretty regular, honestly. For the past several months, it’s usually at least once a week—most often at night after work—where I’ll stop and buy too much food, more than I really need, and then I end up eating all of it in one stretch.

I keep trying to tell myself it was just a bad week or that I’ll get back on track, but when I think about it, I can’t really remember a recent month where it stopped for more than maybe a week or so. It’s not every single day, but it’s consistent enough that I notice it, and I kind of expect it now, which feels awful to say.

As for the feeling part… I’m not totally sure how to separate it out, but it does seem to happen after work a lot, especially when I’m worn down or in my head. Like the night just kind of turns into that before I’ve really talked myself out of it.
When you're having one of these eating episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of how much you're eating or that you can't stop once you start?

Yeah… yes, that’s probably the part that scares me the most, honestly. It doesn’t feel like a normal decision once it’s started. At first I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some of it, or just eat enough to feel full, but then it’s like I keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically.

And the weird thing is I’m not completely unaware, you know? I’m thinking while it’s happening. I’ll literally have this voice in my head like, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” or “You don’t even want this anymore,” but my body just keeps going. I’ll open the next container or unwrap the next thing, and part of me is watching myself do it and feeling upset, but I still don’t stop.

Usually it only ends when the food is gone, or when I feel so uncomfortable that continuing would just make me feel sick. So… yeah, it really does feel like I can’t control how much I’m eating once I’ve crossed that line.
Outside of these eating episodes, do you find yourself feeling down, anxious, or really hard on yourself most days, even when there’s no food involved?

I don’t know… I mean, I’m definitely hard on myself a lot, but it’s hard for me to tell where that ends and where this whole eating thing starts, if that makes sense.

Like, I wouldn’t say I wake up every single day feeling sad for no reason, exactly. Some days I’m just tired or annoyed or stressed in a normal way, and I can go to work and do what I need to do. But I do catch myself kind of criticizing everything I do—how I look, whether I’m being lazy, whether I’m falling behind—stuff like that. It’s not always loud, but it’s there.

Anxious… maybe sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d call it that most days. I don’t want to exaggerate it. It’s more like this low-level pressure in my head, and then after the eating episodes it gets way worse. But outside of those, I guess I’m not totally sure how to separate what’s normal stress from something more than that.
Do you find yourself feeling particularly upset or preoccupied about your body shape or weight, especially in relation to these eating episodes?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I do think about my body, and I don’t always feel great about it, especially after one of those nights, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s the main thing driving it.

After I eat like that, I’ll feel really gross and embarrassed, and then I’ll start looking at myself differently, like my clothes feel wrong or I feel heavier even if that probably doesn’t make sense. But before it happens, I’m not always sitting there thinking, “I hate my body,” or anything that clear. Sometimes it’s more like I just don’t want to think about myself at all.

Weight is… I don’t know. It’s in the background. I notice it, I worry a little, but I’m not weighing myself constantly or planning everything around it. It’s more that the eating episode makes me feel upset with myself, and then my body becomes part of what I’m upset about. Does that make sense?
Do you feel a strong preoccupation or distress about your body shape or weight most of the time, not just after eating episodes?

I don’t think it’s most of the time, no… or at least, not in a really intense way.

Like, I’m aware of my body. I have moments where I don’t like how I look, or I’ll feel uncomfortable in certain clothes, or I’ll catch myself comparing myself to someone, especially if I’m already feeling bad. But it’s not like I spend the whole day obsessing over my weight or checking myself constantly. I don’t think my entire mood is built around the number or anything like that.

It’s more noticeable after I’ve eaten too much, because then everything feels worse and I get this kind of disgusted feeling with myself. But on normal days, I can usually go to work, do my cleaning route, think about other things, talk to people, and not be stuck on my body the whole time.

So… I guess I’d say it bothers me sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it a strong preoccupation most of the time.

Outside of these eating episodes and the feelings that come right after them, do you find that your daily functioning — like work, relationships, or other responsibilities — is significantly affected by your thoughts or mood?

Yeah… I mean, not in a way where I’m missing work all the time or completely falling apart, if that’s what you mean. I still get up and go to my cleaning shifts. I still do what I’m supposed to do, and if there’s a design event or something I said I’d go to, I usually still make myself show up.

But it does affect me, just maybe more quietly. The day after one of those episodes, I’ll be at work pushing the cart around or cleaning bathrooms or whatever, and I’m doing the tasks, but my head is somewhere else. I’ll keep replaying it and feeling embarrassed, like I’m carrying this gross secret around. And then I feel ashamed for being distracted, because it’s not like anyone else knows why I’m acting weird or slower.

With the design stuff, it’s kind of specific. I sketch and keep notes, and sometimes after an episode I’ll write these really harsh journal entries, just dumping everything I’m feeling. Then later I don’t want to even open the journal because I know those pages are in there. So I’ll put off sketching, even if I had an idea, because looking at the notebook feels like having to look at myself from that night again.

So… I’m functioning, technically. I’m showing up. But the next day especially, I’m distracted and ashamed, and it can make me avoid things I actually care about.
Do you feel marked distress about your body shape or weight, even when you’re not having an eating episode?

I don’t think I’d call it marked distress, no. I mean, I do have feelings about my body, and there are days where I’ll put something on and feel uncomfortable or kind of disappointed, and then I’ll change clothes three times and get annoyed with myself. But if you mean like, am I constantly upset about my shape or weight even when nothing happened with eating… I don’t think so.

It’s more like it gets louder after I’ve overeaten. Then I feel really ashamed and my body becomes this thing I focus on, like everything feels wrong. But on a regular day, I can usually move through things without being stuck on it. I might notice my reflection or compare myself for a second, but then I’m back to work or errands or whatever I’m doing.

So… I guess it bothers me sometimes, but not in that big, constant way. It’s not absent, but it’s not the main thing in my head most of the time.

During these eating episodes, would you say you feel a complete loss of control, like you can’t stop eating even if you want to, or is it more that you feel like you shouldn’t be eating that much but still feel in control while you’re doing it?

It feels more like I lose control, honestly. I don’t know if I’d say I’m completely blank or anything, because I am aware of what I’m doing, but once I start, it’s like I keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically.

I’ll even be thinking in my head, like, “Fumi, stop. You have sketches to finish. You don’t need this. Just put it away.” And I’ll mean it when I think it, but then my hand is still opening something else, or I’m still going back for more. It’s like the part of me that knows I should stop is talking, but it’s not actually in charge.

Usually I don’t really stop because I made a calm decision to stop. I stop because the food is gone, or because I feel so uncomfortable that I can’t keep pretending it’s fine. That’s the part that scares me afterward, because during it I keep thinking I’m about to stop, like after this one thing, after this last bite, and then I just… don’t.
Do these eating episodes usually happen after you've been fasting or following a strict diet or eating plan?

I don’t really know. I mean… I don’t think of myself as someone who fasts or follows some strict plan, not in an organized way. I’m not, like, counting every calorie or doing a named diet or anything like that.

Sometimes I’ll tell myself I’m going to “eat better” the next day, or I’ll skip something because I feel bad about what happened before, but I don’t know if that counts as fasting. It’s not usually this clear thing where I’ve been on a strict eating plan and then that directly leads to an episode. At least, I haven’t noticed that pattern.

It feels more messy than that. Like I might have a day where my meals are weird because of work or because I’m distracted, but I wouldn’t say, “Oh, every time I restrict, then it happens.” I’m not sure I could track it that neatly. So… no, not usually after a strict diet, I don’t think. Or if it is connected sometimes, I haven’t really paid attention enough to say that confidently.
Can you think of a specific time when one of these eating episodes happened, and you hadn’t skipped meals or been restricting your food beforehand?

Yeah, I can think of times like that. Not always with, like, an exact date, but a pretty common version is after work. I’ll come home from cleaning, and I’ll already have eaten something normal after my shift, so it’s not like I’ve been starving myself all day or skipped everything.

Like, I’ll have dinner or at least enough food that I know I’m not actually hungry, and then I’ll sit down because I’m tired, or I’ll try to work on a design idea or sketch for something, and if I get stuck, I start feeling restless. Then I’ll go into the kitchen and open something—chips, crackers, whatever’s easy—and at first I tell myself it’s just a little snack while I think.

But a lot of the time I’m not even hungry. That’s the weird part. I can feel that I’m not hungry, like my body isn’t asking for food, but I’ll still keep opening things and eating them. It feels more like I’m tired or frustrated or just stuck in my head, and the eating starts happening anyway. So yeah, there have definitely been episodes where I hadn’t restricted beforehand. I had eaten, and then it still happened.
On average, how many times a week do these eating episodes happen, and have you noticed them happening consistently over a period of at least three months?

I think… on average it’s at least once a week. Sometimes it might be more than that, depending on the week, but the pattern I can say for sure is there’s usually one night where it happens.

A lot of times it’s after work. I’ll be on my way home and stop somewhere, and I’ll buy way more food than I meant to—like more than makes sense for one person for one night—and then when I get home I end up eating all of it in one stretch. Not like a normal meal, more like I just keep going until it’s gone.

And yeah, it’s been going on for several months. I can’t really think of a recent month where it completely stopped. Maybe there are weeks where it doesn’t happen, or it’s not as bad, but I don’t think it’s gone away for more than a week or so at a time. It feels pretty steady, which is embarrassing to say, but… yeah, at least weekly for the past few months.
Would you say that your feelings about your body shape or weight are a major reason you feel so upset after these eating episodes?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do feel bad about my body sometimes, and after it happens I can definitely have thoughts like, “Why did I do that?” or I’ll feel gross or uncomfortable in my clothes or just kind of ashamed. But I don’t know if I’d say my body shape or weight is the main reason I’m upset afterward.

It’s more like… the upset feeling is all tangled together. Part of it is about how my body feels, like being too full or feeling like I messed up. Part of it is the loss of control, like I told myself I wasn’t going to do it and then I did anyway. And then I get mad at myself because it feels wasteful or embarrassing, especially if I bought all this food and ate it alone.

So I guess body and weight thoughts are in there sometimes, but I don’t know if they’re the major reason. I haven’t really separated it out like that before.
Outside of the shame and upset you feel after eating episodes, do you experience marked distress about your body shape or weight on a regular basis, even when you haven't had an episode?

I don’t know if I’d call it “marked,” I guess. Like, I definitely have days where I don’t like how I look, or I’ll notice my clothes fitting a certain way and get kind of self-conscious, but I don’t think I’m sitting around all day constantly distressed about my weight or shape when nothing has happened.

It’s more noticeable after an episode, because then I feel really aware of my body and uncomfortable and embarrassed. On regular days, it comes and goes. I might avoid looking too long in the mirror, or I might compare myself to somebody for a second, but then I’m usually distracted by work or errands or whatever I’m doing.

So… I guess outside of those times, it’s there sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s this major ongoing distress. I haven’t really tracked it that way.
Outside of eating episodes and their immediate aftermath, do you find yourself feeling intense distress or preoccupation about your body shape or weight on a regular basis?

I don’t think so, not in that intense way. I mean, I’m aware of my body, and I can be self-conscious, especially if my clothes feel tight or I catch myself in a mirror at a bad angle or something. But outside of those eating nights and right after, I don’t think I’m regularly consumed by it.

It’s more like background noise sometimes, if that makes sense. Like I might think, “I don’t like how I look today,” or I might compare myself to someone for a minute, but then I’m usually just going to work or cleaning or dealing with whatever else is happening. It doesn’t usually take over the whole day.

After an episode it’s different, because then I feel much more upset and embarrassed and aware of my body. But on normal days, I wouldn’t say it’s an intense preoccupation. At least I haven’t noticed it being like that.
During these eating episodes, would you say you feel like you can't stop eating even when you want to, or do you feel like you're choosing to keep eating even if you know you shouldn't?

Yeah… I think it’s more like I can’t stop, even though technically I know I’m the one doing it, if that makes sense.

Like once I start, it feels like my hand just keeps going to the next thing almost automatically. I’ll be thinking, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” or “You said you were only going to have a little bit,” and I really do mean it in my head. But then I don’t actually stop. I keep opening something else, or going back for more, and it feels like there’s this momentum to it.

It’s not like I’m calmly deciding, “Okay, I choose to keep eating and I’m fine with it.” I usually already know I shouldn’t keep going, and I’m kind of arguing with myself while it’s happening. But the stopping part doesn’t happen until the food is gone, or until I feel so uncomfortable that I basically have to stop. So… I guess it feels less like a choice and more like I lose control once I’ve started.

I’ll keep replaying it and feeling embarrassed, like I’m carrying this gross secret around. And then I feel ashamed for being distracted, because it’s not like anyone else knows why I’m acting weird or slower.

With the design stuff, it’s kind of specific. I sketch and keep notes, and sometimes after an episode I’ll write these really harsh journal entries, just dumping everything I’m feeling. Then later I don’t want to even open the journal because I know those pages are in there. So I’ll put off sketching, even if I had an idea, because looking at the notebook feels like having to look at myself from that night again.

So… I’m functioning, technically. I’m showing up. But the next day especially, I’m distracted and ashamed, and it can make me avoid things I actually care about.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences marked distress regarding body shape or weight, which is a key distinguishing factor between F50.2 (Bulimia Nervosa) and F50.9 (Eating Disorder, Unspecified).
doctor.question: Do you feel marked distress about your body shape or weight, even when you’re not having an eating episode?

target_item.reason: The question is about marked distress or preoccupation regarding body shape or weight outside of eating episodes, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I’d call it marked distress, no. I mean, I do have feelings about my body, and there are days where I’ll put something on and feel uncomfortable or kind of disappointed, and then I’ll change clothes three times and get annoyed with myself. But if you mean like, am I constantly upset about my shape or weight even when nothing happened with eating… I don’t think so.

It’s more like it gets louder after I’ve overeaten. Then I feel really ashamed and my body becomes this thing I focus on, like everything feels wrong. But on a regular day, I can usually move through things without being stuck on it. I might notice my reflection or compare myself for a second, but then I’m back to work or errands or whatever I’m doing.

So… I guess it bothers me sometimes, but not in that big, constant way. It’s not absent, but it’s not the main thing in my head most of the time.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences a sense of loss of control during eating episodes, which is key to differentiating between F50.2 (Atypical Anorexia Nervosa) and F50.9 (Unspecified Eating Disorder), as F50.2 typically lacks the binge eating component with loss of control.
doctor.question: During these eating episodes, would you say you feel a complete loss of control, like you can’t stop eating even if you want to, or is it more that you feel like you shouldn’t be eating that much but still feel in control while you’re doing it?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Control
target_item.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like I keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically, and even while I’m thinking, 'Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,' I don’t actually stop until the food is gone or I feel too uncomfortable.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether, during eating episodes, there is a loss of control and inability to stop eating, which directly matches this symptom.

patient.answer:
It feels more like I lose control, honestly. I don’t know if I’d say I’m completely blank or anything, because I am aware of what I’m doing, but once I start, it’s like I keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically.

I’ll even be thinking in my head, like, “Fumi, stop. You have sketches to finish. You don’t need this. Just put it away.” And I’ll mean it when I think it, but then my hand is still opening something else, or I’m still going back for more. It’s like the part of me that knows I should stop is talking, but it’s not actually in charge.

Usually I don’t really stop because I made a calm decision to stop. I stop because the food is gone, or because I feel so uncomfortable that I can’t keep pretending it’s fine. That’s the part that scares me afterward, because during it I keep thinking I’m about to stop, like after this one thing, after this last bite, and then I just… don’t.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating episodes occur while fasting or during periods of strict dietary restriction, which would support a diagnosis of bulimia nervosa (F50.2).
doctor.question: Do these eating episodes usually happen after you've been fasting or following a strict diet or eating plan?

target_item.reason: The question asks whether episodes usually follow fasting, strict dieting, or a rigid eating plan, but the provided symptom profile does not include any item about dietary restriction or fasting preceding binges.

patient.answer:
I don’t really know. I mean… I don’t think of myself as someone who fasts or follows some strict plan, not in an organized way. I’m not, like, counting every calorie or doing a named diet or anything like that.

Sometimes I’ll tell myself I’m going to “eat better” the next day, or I’ll skip something because I feel bad about what happened before, but I don’t know if that counts as fasting. It’s not usually this clear thing where I’ve been on a strict eating plan and then that directly leads to an episode. At least, I haven’t noticed that pattern.

It feels more messy than that. Like I might have a day where my meals are weird because of work or because I’m distracted, but I wouldn’t say, “Oh, every time I restrict, then it happens.” I’m not sure I could track it that neatly. So… no, not usually after a strict diet, I don’t think. Or if it is connected sometimes, I haven’t really paid attention enough to say that confidently.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating episodes occur in the absence of fasting or dietary restriction, which is a key distinction for diagnosis between F50.2 (Binge Eating Disorder) and F50.9 (Eating Disorder, Unspecified).
doctor.question: Can you think of a specific time when one of these eating episodes happened, and you hadn’t skipped meals or been restricting your food beforehand?

target_item.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
target_item.manifestation: A lot of the time I’m not even hungry, like I might have already eaten after work, but if I’m tired or stuck on a design idea I still start opening snacks and keep going.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about an episode that occurred without prior fasting or restriction; the closest matching profile is eating a large amount despite not being physically hungry or after already having eaten.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I can think of times like that. Not always with, like, an exact date, but a pretty common version is after work. I’ll come home from cleaning, and I’ll already have eaten something normal after my shift, so it’s not like I’ve been starving myself all day or skipped everything.

Like, I’ll have dinner or at least enough food that I know I’m not actually hungry, and then I’ll sit down because I’m tired, or I’ll try to work on a design idea or sketch for something, and if I get stuck, I start feeling restless. Then I’ll go into the kitchen and open something—chips, crackers, whatever’s easy—and at first I tell myself it’s just a little snack while I think.

But a lot of the time I’m not even hungry. That’s the weird part. I can feel that I’m not hungry, like my body isn’t asking for food, but I’ll still keep opening things and eating them. It feels more like I’m tired or frustrated or just stuck in my head, and the eating starts happening anyway. So yeah, there have definitely been episodes where I hadn’t restricted beforehand. I had eaten, and then it still happened.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating episodes occur with a frequency that meets the criteria for bulimia nervosa (F50.2) versus the unspecified feeding or eating disorder (F50.9).
doctor.question: On average, how many times a week do these eating episodes happen, and have you noticed them happening consistently over a period of at least three months?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: For the past several months, there has usually been at least one night each week where I buy too much food after work and eat it all in one stretch. I can’t remember a recent month where it stopped for more than a week or so.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about the average weekly frequency of eating episodes and whether they have occurred consistently for at least three months.

patient.answer:
I think… on average it’s at least once a week. Sometimes it might be more than that, depending on the week, but the pattern I can say for sure is there’s usually one night where it happens.

A lot of times it’s after work. I’ll be on my way home and stop somewhere, and I’ll buy way more food than I meant to—like more than makes sense for one person for one night—and then when I get home I end up eating all of it in one stretch. Not like a normal meal, more like I just keep going until it’s gone.

And yeah, it’s been going on for several months. I can’t really think of a recent month where it completely stopped. Maybe there are weeks where it doesn’t happen, or it’s not as bad, but I don’t think it’s gone away for more than a week or so at a time. It feels pretty steady, which is embarrassing to say, but… yeah, at least weekly for the past few months.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating episodes are associated with marked distress about body shape or weight, which would support a diagnosis of bulimia nervosa (F50.2) over unspecified eating disorder (F50.9).
doctor.question: Would you say that your feelings about your body shape or weight are a major reason you feel so upset after these eating episodes?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically asking whether distress after eating episodes is mainly driven by concerns about body shape or weight, but the symptom profile only covers feeling guilty/disgusted afterward in general and does not include body shape or weight concerns.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do feel bad about my body sometimes, and after it happens I can definitely have thoughts like, “Why did I do that?” or I’ll feel gross or uncomfortable in my clothes or just kind of ashamed. But I don’t know if I’d say my body shape or weight is the main reason I’m upset afterward.

It’s more like… the upset feeling is all tangled together. Part of it is about how my body feels, like being too full or feeling like I messed up. Part of it is the loss of control, like I told myself I wasn’t going to do it and then I did anyway. And then I get mad at myself because it feels wasteful or embarrassing, especially if I bought all this food and ate it alone.

So I guess body and weight thoughts are in there sometimes, but I don’t know if they’re the major reason. I haven’t really separated it out like that before.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's eating episodes are associated with marked distress about body shape or weight, which would support F50.2 (Bulimia Nervosa) over F50.9 (Eating Disorder Not Otherwise Specified).
doctor.question: Outside of the shame and upset you feel after eating episodes, do you experience marked distress about your body shape or weight on a regular basis, even when you haven't had an episode?

target_item.reason: The question asks about regular marked distress about body shape or weight outside of binge-eating episodes, but the symptom profile does not include a body-shape or weight-distress item separate from shame or guilt after episodes.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d call it “marked,” I guess. Like, I definitely have days where I don’t like how I look, or I’ll notice my clothes fitting a certain way and get kind of self-conscious, but I don’t think I’m sitting around all day constantly distressed about my weight or shape when nothing has happened.

It’s more noticeable after an episode, because then I feel really aware of my body and uncomfortable and embarrassed. On regular days, it comes and goes. I might avoid looking too long in the mirror, or I might compare myself to somebody for a second, but then I’m usually distracted by work or errands or whatever I’m doing.

So… I guess outside of those times, it’s there sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s this major ongoing distress. I haven’t really tracked it that way.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences a feeling of being marked distress about body shape or weight that is not tied to eating episodes, in order to differentiate between F50.2 (Bulimia nervosa) and F50.9 (Eating disorder, unspecified)
doctor.question: Outside of eating episodes and their immediate aftermath, do you find yourself feeling intense distress or preoccupation about your body shape or weight on a regular basis?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about regular intense distress or preoccupation with body shape or weight outside of binge-eating episodes, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, not in that intense way. I mean, I’m aware of my body, and I can be self-conscious, especially if my clothes feel tight or I catch myself in a mirror at a bad angle or something. But outside of those eating nights and right after, I don’t think I’m regularly consumed by it.

It’s more like background noise sometimes, if that makes sense. Like I might think, “I don’t like how I look today,” or I might compare myself to someone for a minute, but then I’m usually just going to work or cleaning or dealing with whatever else is happening. It doesn’t usually take over the whole day.

After an episode it’s different, because then I feel much more upset and embarrassed and aware of my body. But on normal days, I wouldn’t say it’s an intense preoccupation. At least I haven’t noticed it being like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences a sense of loss of control during eating episodes, which is key to differentiating between F50.2 (Binge Eating Disorder) and F50.9 (Eating Disorder, Unspecified).
doctor.question: During these eating episodes, would you say you feel like you can't stop eating even when you want to, or do you feel like you're choosing to keep eating even if you know you shouldn't?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Control
target_item.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like I keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically, and even while I’m thinking, 'Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,' I don’t actually stop until the food is gone or I feel too uncomfortable.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether during episodes I feel unable to stop eating versus choosing to continue, which matches loss of control over eating.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think it’s more like I can’t stop, even though technically I know I’m the one doing it, if that makes sense.

Like once I start, it feels like my hand just keeps going to the next thing almost automatically. I’ll be thinking, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” or “You said you were only going to have a little bit,” and I really do mean it in my head. But then I don’t actually stop. I keep opening something else, or going back for more, and it feels like there’s this momentum to it.

It’s not like I’m calmly deciding, “Okay, I choose to keep eating and I’m fine with it.” I usually already know I shouldn’t keep going, and I’m kind of arguing with myself while it’s happening. But the stopping part doesn’t happen until the food is gone, or until I feel so uncomfortable that I basically have to stop. So… I guess it feels less like a choice and more like I lose control once I’ve started.
